- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to under-forecast; increase forecast slightly to align with sentiment momentum.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33) in recent days, model tends to over-forecast; reduce forecast to match sentiment pessimism.  
- Model consistently over-estimates early in the 30-day horizon (especially days 1–5) after sharp price spikes; apply downward bias to first 5 days post-spike.  
- Model under-estimates late in the 30-day horizon (days 25–30) when sentiment is positive; apply upward bias to final 5 days if sentiment remains positive.  
- If sentiment turns positive after a negative streak, model often fails to catch the reversal; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% in the 10–15 day window following sentiment shift.  
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: over-forecasting after strong upward moves, under-forecasting after strong downward moves — apply opposite bias to the 3–5 day window following extreme moves.
